predictedRisks.riskTitle: PAT Defect Discovery Surge Due to Late Testing Coverage Maturation
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Front-end testing coverage matured late with automation resources mobilized only in Sprint 4. PAT early verification has already generated defect and enhancement feedback requiring rework. Additional user-facing defects in form validation logic, chat escalation workflows, admin access controls, MSAL/RBAC implementation, or integrated end-to-end scenarios are likely to surface during formal PAT, increasing rework volume and extending regression effort.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Front-end automation and comprehensive user-path validation were not established early in the delivery lifecycle. Quality debt has accumulated through iterative feedback cycles, with UI-related bugs, in-flight functionality issues, and enhancement requests being added to the backlog at sprint close rather than being prevented through robust early testing.

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Client Review Latency During Demo and PAT Cycles
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project execution model depends on timely client review for sprint demos, early access validation, and PAT acceptance decisions. Given the established pattern of feedback being added to the backlog at sprint close and pending business discussions on escalation requirements, delayed or late-breaking client feedback may create additional rework loops, delay acceptance sign-off, and compress downstream regression and deployment readiness activities.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Agile delivery relies on iterative client validation with limited time buffer. Business and process discussions remain active in late delivery stages (chat escalation requirements, monitoring processes), and the project has no slack to absorb review delays without impacting critical path milestones.

potentialImpact.operations: User training, go-live planning, production support enablement, and hypercare preparation may be delayed awaiting final acceptance

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Compressed Critical Path from PAT Through Deployment

The project requires 45+ days of critical activities within 29 days remaining to the contractual end date. Any issue in testing, integration, or deployment preparation is likely to compress downstream readiness activities or force further go-live delay.
predictedRisks.rootCause: The project is already behind the SOW baseline lifecycle, has substantial high-complexity work remaining (PAT, regression, deployment), and has no visible slack between major final-phase gates. Schedule pressure is high, and the critical path extends beyond the contractual end date without formal extension.
